A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FMA-PO method and AlignDockBench study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original docking and alignment results, runtimes, PoseBusters evaluations, redocking experiments, and component ablations in Table 1 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds comparator experiments, component analyses, physical-quality measurements, and a hydrogen-bond optimization case study.

M1.justification: The flow-matching architecture, harmonic prior, training objective, pose-selection variants, and two-phase coordinate optimization remain unchanged. Appendix B.2 provides additional hydrogen-bond modeling details without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain the same training corpus and 369-pair AlignDockBench, including cross-docking and redocking. The added molecular case study stays within existing pose-refinement coverage; large-scale screening costs are projections, not evaluations on new datasets.

E2.justification: V2 evaluates HarmonicFlow and HarmonicFlow with PO, previously only discussed as related work. Tables S9 and S11 substantially expand comparisons through RDKit-centroid initialization, FitDock LB, and PO-refined Vina, LS-align, and FitDock LB configurations. Original Table 1 comparators remain.

E3.justification: Existing training settings, primary scoring protocol, and 263-molecule PoseBusters subset are retained. Added evaluation designs compare alternative initializers under identical PO hyperparameters, distinguish refinement of all ten candidates from refinement of the selected pose, and introduce strain-energy and clash-count measurements. HarmonicFlow receives an explicit best-of-ten RMSD comparison.

E4.justification: V1 primarily ablates PO, pocket inclusion, and sampling count. V2 adds alternative-initializer controls, individual optimization-loss ablations, Vina-score removal, refinement of other methods, RMSD distributions, strain/clash diagnostics, runtime scaling analyses, and a hydrogen-bond convergence case study.

E5.justification: Table S6 adds descriptive Pearson correlation estimates between runtime and ligand complexity. Existing mean-plus-spread reporting continues; no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Headline comparison scores remain unchanged, but substantial results are added for new comparators, ablations, and diagnostics. Existing values also change: FMA-PO without pocket has mean RMSD 1.456 Å in v1 Table S5 versus 1.88 Å in v2 Table S10. Accurate-and-PoseBusters-valid rates change from 35% to 38% for FMA and 39% to 51% for FMA-PO in v1 Figure S6 versus v2 Figure S11, without documented setting changes.

T1.justification: The flow-matching derivation, harmonic-prior definition, Gaussian-overlap formulas, and internal-energy equations are retained. The added hydrogen-bond discussion supplies mechanistic explanation rather than a new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: template-conditioned flow matching with differentiable refinement, the AlignDockBench contribution, and advantages over docking/alignment baselines, including difficult similarity and flexibility regimes. Additional appendix evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands explanations of hydrogen-bond geometry, FMA initialization quality, PO's usefulness with other generators, and Vina scoring's benefit mainly after refinement. Its runtime discussion identifies CPU refinement as a bottleneck and explicitly limits applicability to ultra-large screening without acceleration.

D1.justification: V2 specifies donor-hydrogen pharmacophore placement, gives precise pointers to borrowed architecture algorithms, and elaborates weight-selection criteria for the existing ten-complex tuning set. It also documents separate CPU/GPU stage timings and cloud-cost assumptions. Existing training hyperparameters and data-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting GenBench3D strain analysis, group-ligand docking, and the GAR Tfase case study. It also develops an empirical comparison with the already-cited HarmonicFlow. Section 2 and the broader research positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains largely verbatim. Local changes include expanded pharmacophore explanations, reorganized Appendix D subsections, updated cross-references, small wording corrections, an acknowledgment, and the conference footer.

P2.justification: V2 adds a detailed model schematic, hydrogen-bond trajectory panels, RMSD distribution and strain-energy plots, and numerous comparison, runtime, and ablation tables. It expands the loss-ablation table, adds the previously reported FMA scores to Table 1, redraws the PoseBusters display, and relocates retained figures.

improvement.justification: V1 only partly isolated the sources of the reported gains. V2's common-refinement initialization controls and loss/scoring ablations substantially strengthen evidence for the distinct contributions of FMA and PO. Physical-quality diagnostics and runtime analysis also clarify practical limitations. Although some revised appendix values remain unexplained, these targeted additions materially improve experimental support and interpretability while retaining the original headline results.
